notes: SSNIT IS NOW CHARGED ON INSURABLE EARNINGS. Contributions are due on insurable earnings, which the Trust bounds at both ends — for 2026 a minimum of GH¢587.80 and a maximum of GH¢69,000 a month. Until now this app charged pensionable pay with no floor and no ceiling. For almost everyone that made no difference and it still makes none: a member of staff paid inside the band contributes exactly what they contributed before. Where it mattered was at the edges. Somebody paid below the floor had too little contributed for them; somebody above the ceiling had too much taken from their pay AND too much paid by the institution. Neither was visible anywhere, because the payslip and the ledger agreed with each other — they were both wrong together. The band is a dated figure like the PAYE bands, under Statutory rates, so a payroll for an earlier month reads the band that applied then. YOUR POSTED MONTHS ARE REVIEWED, NOT REWRITTEN: Statutory returns has a Review posted months button that reads every posted payslip and reports any that contributed on an earning outside the band, and by how much, for the employee and for the institution. It changes nothing. Whether a past month is worth correcting depends on what was already remitted to SSNIT, which the app cannot know. THE AUTHORITY'S OWN FORMS, BESIDE YOURS. Your PAYE Remittance Schedule and WHT Return Schedule are unchanged. Underneath each is now the GRA's own sheet — DT 0107A and DT 110 — in its columns, its order and its captions, so filing becomes transcription rather than working the figures out a second time. Columns the system cannot answer are left blank and NAMED underneath with the reason: the accommodation, vehicle and non-cash benefit columns, because payroll has no benefit-in-kind element, and severance for the same reason. A schedule where every column is filled and one was guessed looks fileable and is not. Four things the sheet asks about an employee can now be recorded: position, residency, secondary employment and whether SSNIT was paid. Leave any blank and the sheet says so rather than choosing for you. SCHEDULES EXPORT TO EXCEL. Every statutory schedule now has Export to Excel beside Print. The amounts arrive as NUMBERS, not text, so the first thing anybody does with a filed schedule — total a column — actually works. THE CURRENCY IS STATED ONCE. Schedules used to print the currency in front of every figure, which on a 28-column sheet said nothing after the first cell and crowded out the numbers. It is now declared once above the grid and the figures are left to be figures. Payslips and vouchers are unchanged. A SCHEDULE OF SUPPLIES BEHIND THE VAT RETURN, for VAT-registered institutions only — nothing changes if you are not registered. The return can now show the supplies behind its totals: what was sold, to whom, on what date, at which treatment and the tax on each. It is read from the invoices and receipts themselves rather than from the accounts, because the ledger records the tax charged and cannot tell a zero-rated supply from an exempt one. It then compares itself against the VAT output account and tells you if the two disagree, so a mis-posting is found before you file. Nothing is assumed: a supply that charged tax is standard-rated by definition, and one that charged nothing with no treatment recorded is reported as such rather than being counted into a box it may not belong in. TWO NEW COLUMNS ARE ADDED AND NO EXISTING DATA CHANGES — this installs straight over the previous version. Please still take a backup first: Backup & Export, Back up now.
